starting_question: Does phosphosugar phosphatase YigL also directly remove PNP, and when does that activity matter?

actual_observations.result: Extracts converted PNP to PN; testing PLP and deleting ybhA argued against an indirect PNP-to-PLP-to-PL-to-PN route.
Six multicopy suppressors were recovered; only YigL was a phosphatase. Purified YigL hydrolyzed PNP (Km 0.83 mM, kcat 1.9/s).

yigL deletion reduced extract PNP phosphatase activity about 30% and increased a small PNP pool fourfold, with near-normal growth. pdxK overexpression plus PN exposed stronger PNP accumulation and growth sensitivity.
YbhA hydrolyzed PNP and partly rescued on overexpression, but its deletion barely affected PNP handling in these conditions.
Under alpha-methylglucoside stress, a yigL deletion was disadvantaged in minimal glycerol medium; requirements differed with medium and stressor.

annotation_consequence: Add direct PNP/PLP phosphatase activity and conditional excess-PNP protection. Retain the established sugar-stress role; normal-state PNP catabolism is not reassigned chiefly to YigL.
experiment_dependence: Published purified-enzyme, extract, genotype, metabolite and growth comparisons; no experiments performed here.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors explicitly tested the indirect route, suppressors and forced PNP load. Cross-paper choice ordering is reconstructed with outcomes known.
verification_scope: 2024 relevant complete results/discussion and assay/genotype methods inspected; 2013 relevant regulation, competition and growth results inspected. Supplements not independently analyzed. Fresh public-record probe documented in raw/live_probe_summary.json.

starting_question: Is measurable succinic-semialdehyde reduction the main physiological job of YihU?

actual_observations.result: Yeast-extract screening yielded SSA/fumarate signals without a clear depleted substrate. Defined reactions established NADH-dependent SSA-to-GHB conversion; fumarate could not be reproduced with the tested defined mixtures.
Exogenous SSA sensitivity and overexpression metabolomics supported stress detoxification. Table1 also showed strong oxidation of 3-hydroxypropanesulfonate, a non-native analog.

SQ-grown cells induced the yih cluster and DHPS oxidation; native active-protein purification/peptide identification and recombinant YihU assigned SLA reductase. SQ dehydrogenase activity was undetected.
Later SLA kinetics showed roughly 42,000-fold greater catalytic efficiency than prior SSA parameters; GAP reduction was undetected. Product-bound structures identified a sulfonate-recognition pocket.

annotation_consequence: Physiological sulfolactaldehyde reductase in sulfoglycolysis, producing DHPS. Earlier SSA reduction is real assay chemistry; a secondary stress contribution is not categorically excluded.
experiment_dependence: Published authentic-product analysis, growth/induction, native purification, recombinant reactions, kinetics and structures. None repeated experimentally here.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Reported experimental pivots are distinguished from my reconstructed two-route source interrogation and current record/arithmetic probes.
verification_scope: 2009 relevant whole results/discussion and reaction methods; 2014 primary main results, enzyme methods and relevant extended-data legends; 2020 accepted manuscript sequence, kinetics, structure and conclusion sections inspected. Supporting spectra/kinetic fits were not reanalyzed.

gene_protein_organism.organism: Escherichia coli; 2000 comparisons include Methanococcus jannaschii, Archaeoglobus fulgidus and Thermotoga maritima enzymes

starting_question: Does inositol-phosphatase activity explain SuhB-dependent growth, or is another protein-specific function required?

actual_observations.result: Three heterologous IMPases were active in transformed extracts but failed growth complementation; catalytically inactive E. coli D87N retained complementation.
Suppressor selection implicated rnc and nusE. Additional Nus mutations, unlike several other translation-defective mutations, rescued suhB phenotypes.
SuhB recruitment required NusB/BoxA. A plasmid reporter required SuhB for antitermination, but endogenous rRNA RNAP occupancy changed only modestly; NusB association depended strongly on SuhB.
Purified SuhB bound NusA-AR2 and rrnG RNA and joined a transcription complex. Weak RNAP contacts and detailed recruitment mechanisms retained uncertainty.

annotation_consequence: Retain genuine IMPase activity while assigning a physiological role in Nus-associated rRNA maturation/ribosome biogenesis. The exact looping/assembly mechanism remains a model; do not transfer the E. coli role to every archaeal IMPase.
experiment_dependence: Published activity-separated complementation, suppressor genetics, RNA-seq/ChIP and physical-interaction assays. No new experiments.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Reported tests support distinct alternatives. My route choices are reconstructed, not an asserted complete author chronology.
verification_scope: 2000 primary abstract only; 2016 suppressor, recruitment, reporter/endogenous comparison, genetic-interaction results and relevant methods/discussion inspected; 2019 relevant binding/reconstitution results/methods and stated limitations inspected. Raw data and earlier 1994 activity paper not independently analyzed.

gene_protein_organism.organism: Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv; heterologous complementation in E. coli

starting_question: Does activity on IMP/FBP establish inositol biosynthesis, or was a preferred PAP substrate omitted?

actual_observations.result: Homology suggested CysQ despite an earlier bifunctional IMPase/FBPase claim. PAP-affinity purification and protein mass/peptide checks improved attribution.
PAP had low-micromolar Km; IMP and FBP catalytic efficiencies were over 1,000-fold lower. A sensitive MS assay was needed; low-PAP linearity and PAPS instability remained limitations.
Expression restored an E. coli cysQ mutant sulfur-growth defect.
Native Mtb deletion work found no inositol requirement in recovered cysQ mutants but explicitly could not exclude acquired suppressors.

annotation_consequence: PAP-preferring CysQ phosphatase rather than primary IMPase/FBPase. Native sulfur-regulatory contribution is supported by biochemical/heterologous evidence but was not directly quantified as Mtb PAP flux here.
experiment_dependence: Published comparative kinetics, product MS, complementation and limited native genetics; no new assays.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors report reconsidering the earlier substrate assignment. Separation of biochemical preference from native-flux proof is my bounded assessment.
verification_scope: 2008 primary relevant full methods/results/discussion inspected. 2010 CysQ deletion, extract-activity and discussion sections inspected; no genome analysis of putative suppressors.

gene_protein_organism.organism: Escherichia coli K-12 and Salmonella enterica

starting_question: Does an authentic mannose-bound structure identify the native substrate of this AGE-fold protein?

actual_observations.result: Purified E. coli and Salmonella proteins lacked AGE activity but interconverted ordinary monosaccharides; a Salmonella H248A structure bound mannose.
E. coli SQ catalytic efficiency was178-fold greater than the earlier mannose value; no G6P conversion was detected at 10 mM.
NMR revealed an additional product. Deuterium exchange and an authentic synthetic reference identified sulforhamnose; starting from each sulfosugar reached the same equilibrium.
Anomer/mutarotase comparisons supported beta-SQ preference. The Salmonella SF complex identified a sulfonate pocket; it is not an E. coli structure.

annotation_consequence: SQ isomerase with sulforhamnose epimerization and strong sulfosugar selectivity; retain ordinary-sugar side activities without identifying them as the chief native role.
experiment_dependence: Published kinetics, product chemistry, anomer experiments and structure; no new assays.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors explicitly revisited product identity and specificity. The lesson about authentic ligand binding versus physiological priority is reconstructed.
verification_scope: 2008 primary abstract inspected; 2021 relevant complete YihS results, comparisons and figure legends inspected. Supporting spectra/kinetic fits not independently reprocessed.
counting_note: Overlap with root/cases.jsonl. Overlapping primary-source elaboration, not another counted gene/function question.

gene_protein_organism.gene: aq_1744 / gpmA label in current deposition
gene_protein_organism.protein: histidine-family phosphatase HFP, PP17; UniProt O67630; PDB 9MMH
gene_protein_organism.organism: Aquifex aeolicus; produced in E. coli

starting_question: Which phosphatase can complete riboflavin synthesis without destroying pathway inputs, and does an apparent extra isomerase activity belong to it?

actual_observations.result: Two of 22 screened proteins supported a staged ARAPDP-dephosphorylation readout; only HFP supported the full one-pot pathway. IMP depleted NADPH and Ru5P.
HFP preparations also isomerized Ru5P/R5P. Extensive purification and 90 C heating slowed but did not eliminate this activity.
Four of five randomly chosen other preparations also isomerized the sugar. MS detected E. coli RpiA, defeating attribution of isomerase activity to HFP.
HFP also hydrolyzed FMN; substrate instability prevented comparative ARAPDP kinetics.

annotation_consequence: HFP is an ARAPDP-phosphatase candidate compatible with the reconstituted pathway, not a demonstrated bifunctional ribose-phosphate isomerase. Native essentiality and exclusivity are not established by this paper.
experiment_dependence: Published coupled-pathway reconstitution, NMR, orthogonal purification, contaminant MS and structures. No native knockout/flux experiment is reported.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: The false extra-activity explanation is explicitly reported. Bounded native-role wording is my assessment rather than adoption of the title essential.
verification_scope: Primary relevant complete results/discussion and reconstitution/NMR/purification methods inspected. Supplement MS identification accepted as reported; its underlying spectra were not reanalyzed. Current PDB polymer records bind HFP to aq_1744/O67630; gpmA is a record label, not independent mutase evidence.

starting_question: Can a disputed cofactor-independent pyruvate decarboxylase annotation be repaired by finding any positive alternative assay?

actual_observations.result: Mechanistic calculations questioned the earlier claim. Two protein preparations showed no detectable pyruvate decarboxylation in coupled ADH, NMR and membrane-inlet MS assays despite a nearly identical crystallized fold.
Bound electron density was modeled as hexanoate but remained an unknown ligand; docking could not determine native chemistry.
Later p-nitrophenyl-ester tests found short-chain esterase activity. pNPA Km was 18.6 mM and efficiency 36 M^-1 s^-1; authors explicitly considered it an unlikely native substrate.

annotation_consequence: Do not retain cofactor-independent PDC as established. Record measured model-ester hydrolysis while leaving the physiological substrate/function unresolved; a positive artificial-substrate assay is not a native-function solution.
experiment_dependence: Published computation plus orthogonal negative decarboxylation assays and later model-substrate kinetics; none repeated here.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors report their mechanistic objection and alternative substrate tests. No specific cause for the original positive PDC result was established here.
verification_scope: 2013 main narrative, modeling assumptions and stated assay outcomes inspected; detailed supplementary assay protocols not independently checked. 2019 complete relevant activity/results/discussion and assay conditions inspected. Original 2011 paper not newly verified.

starting_question: Does a broad pyrimidine-nucleotidase assay identify one constitutive native role?

actual_observations.result: A yjjG thyA mutant failed thymine but retained thymidine utilization in the enriched medium used; yjjG expression restored growth. Deletion retained about 50% extract dUMP phosphatase activity.
A separate study reported protection against supplied noncanonical pyrimidines, reduced BrdU incorporation and stronger 5-FdUMP activity; oxidized natural substrates remained proposed.
Follow-up reproduced the salvage contribution with casamino-acid enrichment, but saw little effect in un-enriched minimal medium; dgt supplied an alternative route.

annotation_consequence: Retain nucleotide hydrolysis, conditional thymine salvage and experimentally tested xenonucleotide protection. Neither phenotype alone establishes the dominant substrate in unchallenged cells.
experiment_dependence: Published genotype, feeding/bypass, complementation and nucleotide-incorporation assays. No endogenous oxidized-substrate measurements verified.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors report different experimental conditions and a later scope correction; the synthesis avoids forcing salvage versus housecleaning into exclusive roles.
verification_scope: 2007 salvage relevant whole results and media methods; 2011 relevant dgt/yjjG comparisons, discussion and medium composition inspected. 2007 housecleaning primary abstract only; publisher PDF access failed.
